query: The Shutter Rope {The stars are coming out, and the dome is still shut. The crank rope has jumped its pulley and is hanging up in the dark of the ribs, well out of anyone's reach. A dozen students with star charts look up at it.|The shutter rope has jumped its pulley again. The caretaker says it does it on clear nights only, out of spite.|Up in the ribs of the dome, in the dark, the rope again. Somebody has chalked an arrow on the floor pointing at it.} Climb the brass ribs {You climb the ribs like a ladder and hook the rope with one foot. The shutter grinds open on a sky full of stars, and the room cheers.|Up the ribs, out along the curve, a grab. The rope comes free and the dome opens with a groan like a waking giant.|The handholds are just where you'd hope. Up, grab, down, and the sky is open before the charts are unrolled.} {Halfway up a rib turns slippery with dew and you come down a lot faster than you went up. The rope stays where it is.|You get a hand to the rope and the pulley bites your fingers. You let go of both.|You climb, reach, miss and hang there by your elbows while someone runs for the caretaker.} Read the charts by lamplight instead {The caretaker comes up an hour later with a hook on a pole. By then you've learned the charts by heart, and the best of the sky has gone behind the hill.|You spread the charts on the floor and plot tonight's route across them instead. It isn't the same; it's not nothing.|You read by lamplight under the shut dome. When it finally opens, the moon is up and drowning half of what you came for.} Step into the dark under the dome {You step into the shadow by the door and out of the shadow in the ribs, grab the rope, and step back down. The dome opens. A dozen star charts lower slowly as their owners stare at you.|Shadow to shadow, up into the dark of the dome and back. The rope slots onto its pulley with a clunk. Someone asks if you can do that for the bell tower.|You don't even put your charts down. A step into the dark, a tug, and the shutter rolls back on the whole sky.}
